step1_analysis.description: This circuit is a passive RC network driven by current sources, likely representing a baseband or second-harmonic termination network used for IMD3 cancellation in the referenced BJT amplifier.

paper_reference.title: A Novel Frequency-Independent Third-Order Intermodulation Distortion Cancellation Technique for BJT Amplifiers

Gain.description: Power or voltage gain of the amplifier

sky130_expected.calculation: For a 1.8V SKY130 NMOS amplifier at 1 GHz, intrinsic gain gm*ro is around 15-20 V/V. A single stage typically yields 10-15 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adjusted down from 30 dB as the paper likely uses a multi-stage or high-gain BJT process, whereas a single SKY130 RF NMOS stage provides less gain.

sky130_expected.calculation: Pout = (Vdd - Vknee)^2 / (2*Ropt). With Vdd=1.8V, Vknee=0.3V, Pout max per device is around 20-50 mW unless heavily parallelized.
sky130_expected.reasoning: 3W requires high voltage (5V in paper) or massive device width. For standard 1.8V SKY130, output power is significantly lower without power combining.

sky130_expected.calculation: Standard core device VDD in SKY130.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 core devices are rated for 1.8V nominal.

Efficiency.description: Power Added Efficiency (PAE) or Drain Efficiency

sky130_expected.calculation: Class AB efficiency typically ranges from 30% to 50% depending on the conduction angle and matching.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Efficiency is largely topology-dependent; 40% is a reasonable expectation for a well-matched Class AB PA in SKY130.

sky130_expected.calculation: fT of SKY130 NMOS is ~40 GHz, so 1 GHz is easily supported.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Target frequency remains the same as the application dictates it.

sky130_expected.calculation: Using second-harmonic or baseband injection/termination in CMOS can yield 10-20 dB cancellation depending on PVT variations.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The cancellation technique's effectiveness is similar in CMOS, though limited by lower intrinsic linearity compared to BJTs.

Network Transfer Impedance.description: Transimpedance of the passive network (Vout / Iin)

sky130_expected.calculation: Depends on the R and C values. Assuming R=50 ohms, 20*log10(50) = 34 dB ohms.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard metric for evaluating the extracted passive sub-circuit.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure the DC operating point, AC transimpedance, and transient response of the extracted passive termination network. Component values are assumed as they were missing from the raw extraction.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for IMD3 Cancellation Passive Network

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Define VDD for completeness
VDD vdd GND 1.8

* DUT: Extracted Netlist (with assumed component values appended for simulation)
I1 n1 GND dc 1m ac 1
R1 n0 GND 50
C1 n0 GND 1p
R2 n0 n1 50
C2 n0 GND 1p
C3 n0 n2 1p
R3 n2 GND 50
I2 n2 GND dc 1m ac 0

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point
op
print v(n0) v(n1) v(n2)
let dc_power = -i(VDD) * 1.8
print dc_power

* 2. AC Analysis (Transimpedance)
ac dec 100 1M 10G
let trans_imp_db = vdb(n0)
let phase = 180/PI * cph(v(n0))

meas ac max_gain MAX trans_imp_db
meas ac bw_freq WHEN trans_imp_db='max_gain-3' FALL=1

* 3. Transient Analysis
tran 10p 10n
meas tran v_max MAX v(n0)
meas tran v_min MIN v(n0)

quit
.endc
.end
